finalText:
I'll start by reading the frozen contract and the usage/IPC code.
The error logger takes `(userDataDir, context, error)`. Next, the IPC handlers, main entry, preload, and the existing usage test style.
I have the contracts. Before writing code I need to check the tsconfig and vitest setup so new files are type-checked and picked up by tests.
Config is clear: `src/main/**` and `src/preload/**` are typechecked under the `node` types, and Vitest picks up `src/**/*.test.ts`. I'll write the tests first, starting with the OAuth module.
Next, the implementation for `oauthUsage.ts`. I'm also fixing two assertions in the test file that depend on the host path separator, and I'm tightening the `Retry-After` parse so a negative value does not get read as a date.
Test edits applied. Now the implementation:
Now the `ingestAccount` addition to UsageService. I'll read the end of its existing test file so I can append tests in the same style.
Now the matching implementation in `UsageService.ts`:
Now the refresher. I'm writing its tests first, with the error logger mocked so the test can inspect exactly what gets logged.
Now the refresher implementation:
One gap: `deps.now()` runs outside the try, so a throw there would reject `refresh()`. I'll make the outer chain total as well.
Refresher done. Next the wiring: the usage barrel exports, the IPC handler, the composition root in `index.ts`, and the preload wrapper.
Now `src/main/index.ts`: the real dependencies go here, and the refresher is passed to the IPC registration.
Last wiring piece is the preload wrapper:
Wiring is in. Running the tests and the typecheck now.
All 56 test files pass (1092 tests) and typecheck is clean. Now the build:
The build fails in `src/renderer/usage/useUsage.ts`, which is outside my scope. Typecheck passed a few minutes ago, so I'll re-check whether that file is changing underneath me.
The renderer file was modified at 18:37, and typecheck now passes, so another change is in progress in that area. I'll re-run the build against the current state.
Build passes. I'll do a final vitest run, since the renderer changed after my first run, and check my new files for line count and stray `console` calls.
SUMMARY:
- Manual usage refresh is in place in the main process: `IPC.usageRefresh` calls Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint with the local Claude token and feeds `UsageService.ingestAccount`. Nothing polls it.
- New `oauthUsage.ts` reads the credentials file and performs the request. It maps every failure to a `UsageRefreshError` and never puts the token in an error, log, or result.
- New `usageRefresh.ts` provides single-flight, a 5 s floor, and a 429 cool-down that makes no request. It never throws and logs unexpected errors through `logMainError` with the token redacted.
- The token never crosses IPC. The preload `refreshUsage()` wrapper is added, and the preload typecheck error is gone.
- `npx vitest run` passes (56 files, 1092 tests), `npm run typecheck` is clean, and `npm run build` passes.

FILES CHANGED:
- src/main/usage/oauthUsage.ts (new)
- src/main/usage/oauthUsage.test.ts (new)
- src/main/usage/usageRefresh.ts (new)
- src/main/usage/usageRefresh.test.ts (new)
- src/main/usage/UsageService.ts (added `ingestAccount`)
- src/main/usage/UsageService.test.ts (added `ingestAccount` tests)
- src/main/usage/index.ts (new exports)
- src/main/app/ipcHandlers.ts (`usageRefresher` dep, `IPC.usageRefresh` handler)
- src/main/index.ts (real deps composed, refresher passed to IPC)
- src/preload/index.ts (`refreshUsage()`)

COMMANDS RUN + RESULT:
- `npx vitest run`: pass, 56 files / 1092 tests, 0 failed (run twice; the second run was after the renderer had changed)
- `npm run typecheck`: pass, 0 errors
- `npm run build`: first run failed with TS6133/TS2739 errors in `src/renderer/usage/useUsage.ts`, which another change was editing at the time (outside my scope). Re-run after that file settled: pass.

NOT DONE:
- `ingestAccount` with unchanged windows does not refresh `updatedAt`; it follows the existing `ingest` convention and emits only on change. The spec's literal "updatedAt = now" would conflict with "emit only on change", so say if you want it changed.
- The refresh logic is on `createUsageRefresher(...).refresh()`, not on `UsageService.refresh(deps?)`. The spec was ambiguous here; `UsageService` only gained `ingestAccount`.
- The 10 s timeout is asserted by checking that an `AbortSignal` is passed and that timeout errors map to `network`. There is no real 10 s timer test.
- No renderer button or UI calls `refreshUsage()` yet; the renderer is out of scope.
